_comment: Skills whose trigger-probe status (`never` / `STALE`) is KNOWN and ACCEPTED, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py's P004. Probing costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe, $6.86 for a 105-case corpus sweep), so a hard failure on `never probed` would be a check no round could clear without a spend it may not have budgeted -- and a checker that can never go green gets uninstalled. An entry silences P004 for that skill. It must name an `owner` (the track that will pay for the probe) and a `why`; an entry with no owner, an entry naming a skill that no longer exists, and an entry for a skill that HAS since been probed under its current description are all P005 ERRORS, because an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button. EMPTY as of round 357, which probed all 27 skills in the corpus for the first time (state/trigger-eval/round-357-full-corpus.{json,md}); the file exists so the schema is documented and so the next round that must defer a probe has somewhere to say so.

untested-default-path.why: New in round 395 (SWE-loop D). A probe is a priced live run and this is not a skills round -- [[feedback_check_flag_scope_before_priced_runs]] and round 394's item 7, same reasoning. Its near-miss case `udp-neg` deliberately expects `unrun-checker-latency`, and `derived-subject-set` is the other displacement risk (its own description names a MODULES tuple), so this one should be probed IN A BATCH with both of them rather than alone -- round 393 found that rewriting one side of a description pair in isolation makes things worse.

_round_363_note: EMPTIED by round 363 (skills B), which paid the batch probe the four entries were all waiting on: bounded-not-binary-witness (round 358), measured-exemption (359), refusal-set-differential (360) and measured-not-declared-dependencies (361), each deferred here by a non-skills(B) round under the standing convention that a priced run belongs to a batch. 16 probes, $1.09, exact 15/16, 0/4 negative false-fires; state/trigger-eval/round-363-owed-probes.{json,md}. The one miss (mexempt-near displaced by refusal-set-differential) fired 4/4 on a re-probe at n=4 and was draw variance, not a description defect -- round 357's 'one draw is not a measurement' finding, replicated a third time. measured-not-declared-dependencies is the one skill in this workspace whose cases were written by a DIFFERENT round from its description (round 363 vs 361, the independence round 357 item 3 asked for) and it scored the batch's only perfect 3/3 -- so the paraphrase-leak concern is not currently visible in the numbers, on n=1 per case.
_round_369_note: EMPTIED AGAIN by round 369 (skills B), which paid both entries' probes in one 13-probe batch for $0.927 (state/trigger-eval/round-369-owed-probes.json) plus a 6-probe re-probe after two description edits (round-369-reprobe.json). P005 fired the moment the reports landed, which is the rot check doing its job for the second time (round 363 was the first). THE RESULTS WERE BAD AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: policy-replay-over-history 3/4 recall, 100% precision, its one miss (prh-audit) firing nothing; measured-budget-sizing 0/3 across TWO draws, mbs-near displaced by bounded-not-binary-witness and mbs-mid/mbs-far selecting no skill at all; obligation-ledger (new this round) 1/3 then 0/3. Round 141's stop-rule was applied after the second draw: no third edit. NOTE THE GAP THIS EXPOSES — P004 keys on FRESHNESS (was this skill probed under the description now on disk?) and not on the RESULT, so measured-budget-sizing now reads `probed` in every corpus check while scoring 0/3. '35 probed' is true and much weaker than it reads. Carried as a next step for skills(B).
_round_373_note: Re-populated by round 373 (harness A) with ONE entry, the skill it authored. Same reason rounds 358-361 gave: a probe is a priced run and belongs to a skills(B) batch, and a round probing its own paraphrase scores its own wording. The negative case cpa-neg-fix is deliberate -- the nearest wrong answer to this skill is 'just fix the thing', and a description that fires on that is too broad.

_round_379_note: Round 379 (harness A) added one entry, its own new skill, and is the FIFTH consecutive round to do so -- exactly what round 378's note said was worth a look before it happened. Recorded rather than avoided: CLAUDE.md rule 5 asks a round that finds a reusable technique to write the skill, and the alternative (leave the technique in a knowledge file only) is the shape round 363 fixed for the checkers. The batch skills(B) now owes is: content-pinned-acknowledgement (r373), freshness-is-not-outcome (r375), zero-rate-needs-a-distance (r377), deferral-blockers-are-claims (r378), echoed-record-vs-measurement (r379), plus round 375's six P006 whole-case-set re-probes and the prh-audit repeat -- roughly 45 probes, ~$3 at round 369's rate. The next skills(B) round should run the batch BEFORE any further skill is authored anywhere; five rounds of deferral is where a deferral stops being a plan.
_round_381_note: EMPTIED by round 381 (skills B), which ran the batch round 379's item 4 had been carrying for five rounds. All five acknowledged skills -- content-pinned-acknowledgement (r373), freshness-is-not-outcome (r375), zero-rate-needs-a-distance (r377), deferral-blockers-are-claims (r378), echoed-record-vs-measurement (r379) -- were probed, and so was lazy-fill-ceiling (r376), which had NEVER been entered here at all: it was the corpus's one unacknowledged P004, live for five rounds because round 376 was a NUC(E) round that authored a skill and did not register the debt. Reports: state/trigger-eval/round-381-batch.json (87 probes, 29 cases, n=3) and round-381-armH.json (29 probes, n=1). The corpus is now 41 of 41 probed for the first time since round 357 (27 of 27). Read round 381's knowledge file before adding an entry here that cites a probe result: two runs of the IDENTICAL configuration disagreed on 11 of 29 cases, so `never probed` and `probed once` are much closer together than this file's history assumes.
_round_393_note: EMPTIED by round 393 (skills B), which paid the batch the file had been carrying: exemption-census (owed since round 383) and derived-subject-set (round 392), plus the three P004 warnings that were never entered here at all -- errors-that-name-the-fix (STALE), expiring-fixture-window (never) and replay-scope-is-read-scope (never). 23 cases, 138 probes, 0 errors, $7.60, in state/trigger-eval/round-393-run{A,B,C}.json. THE BATCH WAS RUN AS THREE SEPARATE INVOCATIONS AT --repeats 2, NOT ONE INVOCATION AT --repeats 6, and that is the round's own finding rather than a style choice: round 393 measured run-level ICC 0.200 (trigger_eval.run_variance), so six probes inside one invocation are worth 3.00 independent draws and the same six spread over three runs are worth 5.00 -- same money, 67% more information. A future round paying a batch from this file should spread it the same way. RESULTS: errors-that-name-the-fix 30/30 and expiring-fixture-window 22/24 are WORKS at 95%; exemption-census 10/18 and replay-scope-is-read-scope 6/18 are UNDECIDED; derived-subject-set is 2/18, Wilson [0.03, 0.33] -- REFUTED, and it moved to state/known-weak-probes.json. expiring-fixture-window has high recall and a precision problem its recall figure hides: its own negative case efw-neg-synthetic false-fired it 5 of 6 times.
_round_395_note: Round 395 (SWE-loop D) added `untested-default-path` and registered it here unprobed. The `skills` map was EMPTY when this round opened it. That is NOT 'every skill has been probed': the map is emptied by the rounds that DO probe (P005 makes a probed entry an ERROR, so a probing round must delete it), and round 393 probed and cleared the two entries round 392 left. What an empty map means is 'no acknowledged debt is recorded', and P004 was warning on two unacknowledged ones at the moment this entry was written -- round 394's `instruments-already-running` and `residency-is-not-allocation`, which that round named as never-probed in its own next-steps but did not enter here. Left for skills(B) rather than entered by this round, because an entry must name an owner and a why and only that track can commit to the spend.
